subject: BrightWave go-live: ingress forecast, quota exception & playbook asks
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@brightwavehealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@brightwavehealth.com
Date: 2026-10-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: BrightWave onboarding: initial traffic estimates and ask

Hi Kim / Marissa —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this week. Per our internal planning, we expect to start a staggered rollout of the new assistant on 2026-11-01 and hit peak QA traffic during the first 72 hours of the public launch. Attached is a first-pass estimates workbook (BrightWave_estimates.xlsx) and a draft mutual action plan (MAP_draft_GW_v2.docx).

High-level asks from our side:
- Temporary quota increase to support ~8.5k requests/min at peak for 72 hours starting 2026-11-01.
- A canary window with a 25% subset at 2026-10-28 to validate routing and cold-cache behavior.

To help Redwood size resources we included per-endpoint expected QPS and average tokens per request in tab "launch_profile" of the workbook. Can you confirm what product/config changes you need from our side (model pinning, headers, routing hints)?

Best,
Sarah
Director, Product
BrightWave Health

Date: 2026-10-07T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightWave onboarding: initial traffic estimates and ask

Thanks Sarah — useful workbook, appreciate the detail. Looping in Marissa & Karthik to scope the quota exception and technical playbook. A few quick clarifying asks from product/sales to make the exception request actionable:

1) Confirm expected peak window (start/end) in UTC and timezone of your user base.
2) For each endpoint please add: expected avg tokens per response, expected calls/sec during peak, and % of traffic that uses streaming.
3) Do you plan to pin a model version for the launch? If yes, which model and quantization profile? Pinning affects compatible fallback options.
4) Any regulatory requirements for data residency for the pilot region?

I've attached a lightweight inbound-forecast-template.csv for you to drop numbers into — will make it faster to validate. On the Redwood side, Marissa will own capacity approvals and Karthik will own the technical runbook for routing/fallbacks. Connor will coordinate any Dedicated pool proposals.

Next steps: once we have the CSV populated we'll convert to a formal exception request and a short ops playbook for run-of-show.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@brightwavehealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightWave onboarding: initial traffic estimates and ask

Quick technical readout after a scan of the workbook and a chat with infra:

- Proposed short-term approach (recommended):
  * 72-hour quota exception: 9k req/min peak (to give 6% buffer to their 8.5k ask). Exception id: RDW-EX-238 (provisional).
  * Canary: 25% traffic on 2026-10-28 for 4 hours during off-peak; observe cold-starts and KV cache hit-rate.
  * Fall back policy: route to a slightly smaller, cheaper variant (same family, 8-bit) if latency > 800ms for >5% of tokens over a 5m window.

- Questions for BrightWave (need answers in the CSV):
  1) Median/95th latency SLA target for the assistant (ms).
  2) Are you okay with a transparent model fall-back (we'll signal in logs + header)?
  3) Any plan for scheduled bursts outside the 72-hour window?

- Product ask / roadmap note for PMs:
  * Need a temporary toggle to enable "soft-burst" for hosted customers that: automatically ups allotment for a bounded window and adds an operational flag to the console. This would avoid ad-hoc manual exceptions for similar launches.

I'll stitch a 1-page runbook (capacity-runbook.pdf) and a short checklist for preflight. If Marissa approves the provisional exception I'll raise the formal change ticket to infra.

–Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: capacity-runbook.pdf (pdf)

From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@brightwavehealth.com>

Date: 2026-10-08T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightWave onboarding: initial traffic estimates and ask

Kim, Karthik —

Thanks for the fast turn. We updated the CSV with the requested fields and set the peak window UTC 2026-11-01T15:00:00Z to 2026-11-01T19:00:00Z (first 4 hours public launch).

Answers:
- Median SLA target: 300ms; 95th < 900ms.
- Transparent fallback is OK as long as we get a post-launch report on any fallbacks that occurred.
- No planned bursts outside the launch window for now.

We can sign an SOW for the managed exception once Redwood confirms the exception id and playbook. Can you also confirm whether Redwood will provide a short post-mortem report template we can use?

Forwarding your runbook request to our ops team — will share the signed MAP once ready.

Best,
Sarah

Team —

Summary: BrightWave (RDW-4578) requests a bounded quota increase for public launch on 2026-11-01. Karthik recommends RDW-EX-238 (9k req/min, 72h). They have provided filled CSV and confirmed latency targets.

Asks:
- Infra: please triage/approve RDW-EX-238 — need allocation and burst config (+ rollback window).
- Product: quick review of the "soft-burst" toggle ask; would be very helpful to prevent manual exceptions in future.
- SRE/Ops: review capacity-runbook.pdf and confirm monitoring dashboards/alert thresholds (esp. fallback count, 95th latency, KV cache miss rate).

Related artifacts: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2389 (runbook + tickets)

Timeline: please respond with approvals or blocking comments by EOD 2026-10-09 to meet launch prep windows. If approved I'll convert RDW-EX-238 to a formal infra change request and schedule the canary on 2026-10-28.
